title: Visualizer: JSON In, Trusted UI Out
description: A repository walkthrough of how Pi turns a constrained artifact spec into a validated, rendered page.

components.job: Teaches the agent to inspect evidence, read the contract, choose nodes, and emit JSON.
Registers create_visual_artifact and delegates creation to the installed CLI.
Defines executable Zod validation, resource limits, and the agent-facing node manifest.
Parses, validates, checks Mermaid, safely inlines allowed file sources, writes the bundle, and starts serving.
Serves the exported Next.js shell plus live artifact JSON and assets.
Fetches and parses the saved spec, then dispatches every node type to a trusted adapter.

boundaries.title: Agent → tool
boundaries.description: The model supplies VisualArtifactSpec JSON—not React, JSX, routes, CSS, or full HTML.

boundaries.title: CLI → disk
boundaries.description: Shared schema, resource preflight, and Mermaid parsing run before artifact.json is written.

boundaries.title: Disk → browser
boundaries.description: ClientArtifactLoader bounds the response and parses it again with VisualArtifactSpecSchema.

boundaries.title: Node → UI
boundaries.description: componentRegistry maps the discriminated node type to a repository-owned adapter.

boundaries.title: Local files
boundaries.description: Pi grants no --allow-read; relative file-tree sources must remain inside the canonical project root.

props.content: Visualizer is a local presentation layer for agents. Pi describes content with a small typed JSON vocabulary; the repository—not the model—owns validation, storage, layout, styling, and interaction.

props.title: The Repository at a Glance
props.deck: Four runtime faces surround one shared contract.

props.code:
skill/          agent instructions and composition guidance
pi-extension/   thin Pi tool wrapper
shared/         executable artifact + annotation contracts
cli/            validate, create, serve, open, publish
app/            Next.js static shell, loaders, renderer, adapters
worker/         optional Cloudflare/R2 public runtime
props.title: Mental model
props.caption: Start in shared/ for the language, cli/ for the write boundary, and app/ for what users see.
Each layer has a narrow handoff; arbitrary generated UI code never crosses one.

props.title: How a Person Generates an Artifact with Pi
props.deck: The person asks in natural language; Pi performs the contract-driven assembly.

items.text: Ask Pi for a visual artifact
items.note: Example: “Walk me through this repository using a visual artifact.”

items.text: Pi inspects source and skill guidance
items.note: For architecture work, the skill pipeline collects facts, chooses a thesis, and plans the visual structure.
visual-artifact contract exposes supported nodes, props, data requirements, and resource limits.
It selects semantic nodes such as text, Mermaid, tables, flows, and code blocks.
The extension sends JSON through stdin to visual-artifact create - --project <cwd> --json.
The CLI writes the bundle, starts the local renderer if needed, and returns /artifacts/<project>/<slug>/.

props.title: What Pi conceptually sends
props.caption: The actual tool parameters mirror the root spec and add projectPath only for project-name derivation.

props.title: The End-to-End Spec Flow
props.deck: Two validation passes guard a live-JSON rendering path.

props.caption: Creation runs left to right; browser rendering then fetches the saved JSON and dispatches trusted adapters.
props.code:
flowchart LR
  U["Person prompt"] --> P["Pi agent"]
  S["skill/SKILL.md"] -. guidance .-> P
  C["visual-artifact contract"] -. node vocabulary .-> P
  P -->|VisualArtifactSpec| T["create_visual_artifact"]
  T -->|stdin to create command| CLI["CLI create"]
  SC["shared executable schema"] --> CLI
  CLI --> V{"Valid?"}
  V -->|no| E["Return validation error"]
  V -->|yes| B["Write artifact bundle"]
  B --> A["artifact.json"]
  B --> SRV["CLI static and live JSON server"]
  SRV --> SH["Next.js static shell"]
  SRV --> J["artifact JSON endpoint"]
  SH --> L["ClientArtifactLoader"]
  J --> L
  L -->|bounded fetch and Zod parse| R["VisualArtifactRenderer"]
  R --> REG["componentRegistry"]
  REG --> AD["Trusted adapters"]
  AD --> PAGE["Polished artifact page"]

items.title: Pi tool
items.body: Strip projectPath from spec and invoke CLI

props.caption: The shortest runtime path. The same spec is validated before persistence and again before rendering.

props.title: Contracts That Keep It Safe and Predictable
props.deck: The important architecture is in the boundaries, not the number of components.

props.caption: Validation is deliberate at both system boundaries.

props.code:
~/.local/share/visual-artifact/
├── app/out/                         # installed static renderer
└── artifacts/<project>/<slug>/
    ├── artifact.json                # validated VisualArtifactSpec
    ├── annotations.json             # optional persisted threads
    └── assets/                      # optional sidecars

Page: /artifacts/<project>/<slug>/
JSON: /artifacts/data/artifacts/<project>/<slug>/artifact.json
props.title: Bundle and URL contract
props.caption: Source development may use the repository's artifacts/ directory; installed use defaults to the local data root.

props.title: Where to Start When Changing It
props.deck: These hotspots concentrate the mental model.

props.caption: The shared contract is the handshake; path math and registry dispatch are other key single sources of truth.

props.content: Bottom line: Pi decides what the page says; the contract limits how it can say it; the CLI makes the result durable; the renderer makes it polished.
